context:
Both charts are inline SVG components (consistent with existing
QueryTimingChart pattern). No external charting library needed for
these two chart types - the math is simple and SVG gives full control
over log scale rendering.

Log scale: manually compute SVG x-positions from log2(speedup).
Render grid lines at 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x. Label them.

Diverging bar: sort queries by abs(delta_pct) descending so the most
impactful queries appear at top. Include a summary line: "N queries
faster, M queries slower, median delta: ±X%".
description:
Post-launch audit (2026-04-14) found that the explorer compare view
ships only 2 inline SVG components (grouped bar chart + simple ratio
table) while the CLI offers 15 chart types. The most strategically
important gap for the "dynamic comparison tool" claim is the absence
of charts that make per-query performance deltas legible at a glance:

  1. Normalized speedup chart (log scale, baseline-relative) - answers
     "how much faster/slower is platform B vs platform A per query?"
     The current grouped bar chart doesn't normalize, so a 1ms vs 2ms
     delta looks the same as a 100ms vs 200ms delta.

  2. Diverging bar chart (per-query improvement/regression) - answers
     "which queries got faster and which got slower?" A positive/negative
     bar per query makes regressions immediately obvious. The CLI's
     `diverging_bar` chart type is the primary tool for this.

These two charts close the most visible CLI parity gap and directly
support the compare view's core UX claim.

A phase breakdown (stacked load vs query time) and percentile ladder
are valuable but deferred - they require phase timing fields that are
not yet in the manifest.

anti_patterns.dont: default to the slowest result as baseline
anti_patterns.why: speedup is conventionally measured relative to the alternative, not the worst option

anti_patterns.dont: pull in a charting library (D3, Chart.js, Recharts)
anti_patterns.why: bundle size and dependency overhead aren't justified for 2 chart types

anti_patterns.dont: use linear scale for the speedup chart
anti_patterns.instead: log scale is required for legibility
anti_patterns.why: OLAP deltas span orders of magnitude

preserves.behavior: Compare view URL format - chart selection is UI state, not URL state (no new query params needed)
Existing grouped bar chart - it is the default for 3+ result comparisons and remains accessible via the chart selector
Null-safety: if geomean_ms is missing, disable normalized speedup with a clear message

work_units.notes:
Log scale is important because OLAP query deltas span orders of
magnitude. A linear scale makes small queries illegible when one
large query dominates.

Bar color: green (speedup > 1), red (speedup < 1), neutral (= 1).
Log scale axis labels: 0.1x, 0.25x, 0.5x, 1x, 2x, 4x, 10x.
work_units.summary: Implement NormalizedSpeedupChart: speedup = baseline_ms / this_ms per query, log-scale horizontal bars, green/red for faster/slower. Baseline = first selected result.

work_units.notes:
Convention: red bars = regression (slower than baseline), green bars =
improvement (faster). Magnitude-sorted by abs(delta) so the biggest
changes are at the top. Match CLI diverging_bar semantics.
work_units.summary: Implement DivergingBarChart: delta_ms = this_ms - baseline_ms per query, horizontal diverging bars centered at 0, % change labels, sorted by abs(delta).
Add chart selector to Compare.tsx: toggle between Grouped Bar, Normalized Speedup, Diverging Bar. Default Normalized Speedup for 2-result; Grouped Bar for 3+.
Add baseline selector for normalized speedup chart: when comparing 3+ results, a dropdown lets the user pick which result is the baseline. Default to the fastest (lowest geomean_ms) result.
